evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Smells Like Teen Spirit': Cobain said he was trying to write the ultimate pop song and was trying to rip off Pixies, naming their soft-loud dynamics. Wikipedia's article on 'Surfer Rosa' reports him saying he had heard songs on it like ones he had written and discarded.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen for the volume change. In a Pixies song the verse is quiet, bass and a thin guitar and a muttered vocal, and then the chorus explodes. 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' does exactly this: a quiet, bass-led verse with Cobain half-singing, then the whole band hitting the chorus at full force. Cobain said out loud that this was the part he took.

explanation: Kurt Cobain said that when he wrote 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' he was trying to copy Pixies, especially the way their songs went quiet and then suddenly very loud. It is one of the plainest statements of influence on the whole map, and it describes a technique rather than a mood. Cobain then hired Steve Albini, who had recorded the Pixies album he admired.
